reviewer: Codex human_batch_delivery subagent, machine-assisted independent source/overlay inspection
source_decode_method: Sequential OpenCV original-video decode; source RGB samples and native geometry rendered at exact original IDs using runtime02 Predictions/draw_prediction

visual_findings.detail: Across standing, walking, turning and table-tipping samples, the projected native human remains on the source person with plausible head/torso/arm/leg placement. No gross camera-axis flip, horizontal mirroring, wrong-person tracking, scale explosion, missing limb or scene-wide offset is apparent in these nine samples.

Frames109/219/328/438/547 show changing body direction and foot placement following the walking person. Frames657/766 show the body returning to and bending over the desk. The fixed native body is narrower than loose clothing, which does not by itself demonstrate an alignment failure.

Frames0/657/766/876 include table occlusion. The cyan rendering overlays the original image without a reconstructed-object depth compositor, so visible cyan through the table is not proof of a wrong human depth or proof of physical contact. Hidden limbs, hands, foot-floor contact, penetration and shared object scale are not accepted by this inspection.

Nine image samples and complete finite output coverage do not prove smooth motion on every intermediate frame. The actual EP11 hand movie, hand candidate boundary checks and selected-candidate record still need the separate pilot gate.

raw_fit_diagnostic_interpretation: Difference from raw SAM prediction, not ground-truth or hidden-reference reconstruction error
operational_baseline_conclusion: The longer EP11 baseline passes this read-only operational source/geometry/coverage review. Together with EP16 it supports continuous all-30 baseline generation; retain pending quality and require the separate complete hand/candidate gate before registering accepted reconstruction quality.
